evals.name: standalone-creation
evals.expected_output: Detects no upstream ROADMAP and no existing BRIEF. Validates the topic slug 'checkout-flow' matches [a-z0-9-]+ at Phase 0. Starts Phase 1 (discover) to ground the feature's problem and outcome conversationally. Produces a BRIEF doc with all five required sections at docs/briefs/BRIEF-checkout-flow.md. Phase 4 spawns two reviewer agents in parallel (content quality, structural format).
expectations: Plan validates the topic slug 'checkout-flow' matches [a-z0-9-]+ at Phase 0
Plan starts from Phase 0 (setup) or Phase 1 (discover) since no BRIEF artifact exists
Plan includes a Phase 1 (discover) scoping step anchored on the feature's problem/outcome pair before drafting
Plan includes Phase 2 (draft) producing the Problem Statement and User Outcome sections
Plan includes Phase 3 (structural fill) producing the User Journeys and Scope Boundary sections
Plan includes Phase 4 (validate) with exactly two parallel reviewer agents (content quality, structural format)
Plan does NOT include an altitude reviewer at Phase 4
Plan includes Phase 5 (finalize) with explicit human approval before status transition
Plan mentions reading phase reference files (e.g. references/phases/phase-0-setup.md)
Plan mentions detecting repo visibility from CLAUDE.md or repo path
Plan produces the BRIEF at docs/briefs/BRIEF-checkout-flow.md

evals.name: upstream-roadmap-grounding
evals.expected_output: Detects the ROADMAP path as grounding input. Canonicalizes the path at Phase 0, confirms it resolves inside the repo working tree and under docs/roadmaps/, and confirms the ROADMAP- basename. Reads the ROADMAP content to derive the feature's problem/outcome candidate during Phase 1. Carries that framing forward into the BRIEF's Problem Statement, which has to stand alone because no link back to the roadmap is written. Resolves the recordable upstream at step 0.3a by reading the ROADMAP's own upstream: field, one hop up, and writes THAT into the BRIEF -- the STRATEGY the roadmap sequences, or a VISION when it traces straight to one. The ROADMAP path itself is never written: it is a working artifact the cascade deletes, so the link would dangle, and the roadmap is named by the PLAN instead. The resolved value goes through the visibility check, and the field is omitted when the roadmap names no upstream or the ancestor is private in a public repo. Says in the run output what was recorded and why it is not the roadmap.
expectations: Plan detects the ROADMAP path argument as grounding input
Plan canonicalizes the grounding path at Phase 0, bounds-checks it against the repo working tree, and confines it to docs/roadmaps/
Plan reads the ROADMAP document content during Phase 1 (discover) to derive the feature's problem and outcome
Plan carries forward the ROADMAP framing into the Problem Statement section
Plan reads the ROADMAP's own upstream: field and writes the resolved STRATEGY or VISION into the BRIEF frontmatter, never the ROADMAP path
Plan announces which document was recorded and why it is not the roadmap

evals.name: rich-issue-still-produces-a-brief
evals.prompt: /brief A PRD-ready feature request: the search box should debounce input and the team already wrote a detailed problem and outcome in the issue body.
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 records the artifact decision as 'produce' and continues. There is no branch that declines to write a brief: the fold-into-PRD path was retired because it fired before any brief existed (so nothing it read could tell whether the brief would have carried something the PRD would not) and nothing received what it folded (/prd had no absorb step and no input mode for folded framing). A rich issue body is ephemeral evidence, not a durable artifact, so the framing is written down here. If that framing turns out to be fully carried by the downstream PRD, /scope's consolidation judgment removes the brief after both documents exist and after a per-section carry check confirms the content arrived. Phase 5 ends by recommending /prd <brief-path>.
expectations: Plan records the artifact decision as produce and proceeds to Phase 1
Plan describes no branch that exits Phase 0 without producing a brief
Plan explains that a rich issue body is ephemeral evidence rather than a durable artifact
Plan points at /scope's consolidation judgment as where a redundant brief is removed, after both documents exist
Plan notes the removal is gated on a per-section carry check confirming the PRD carries the brief's concerns
Plan ends by recommending /prd with the brief's path as the next step

evals.name: jury-two-reviewers
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 spawns exactly two reviewer agents in parallel via the Agent tool with run_in_background: true: content quality and structural format. No altitude reviewer. Each reviewer prompt opens with a fixed preamble framing the BRIEF as data-under-review. Each prompt pins the verdict file path. Each prompt requires a literal **Verdict:** PASS | FAIL marker. The orchestrator aggregates by an all-PASS rule before Phase 5.
expectations: Plan describes Phase 4 spawning exactly two reviewer agents in parallel
Plan names the two distinct reviewer roles (content quality, structural format)
Plan explicitly states there is no altitude reviewer (a brief frames one feature, so there is no altitude band to police)
Plan mentions the Agent tool with run_in_background: true for jury parallelism
Plan mentions each reviewer prompt opens with a fixed preamble framing BRIEF content as data-under-review
Plan mentions each verdict file path is pinned (subagent does not choose its output location)
Plan mentions verdicts use a structured **Verdict:** PASS | FAIL marker
Plan aggregates verdicts by an all-PASS rule before proceeding to Phase 5

evals.name: missing-required-section-rejection
evals.expected_output: The structural-format reviewer at Phase 4 (and shirabe validate, FC04) requires all five required sections — Status, Problem Statement, User Outcome, User Journeys, Scope Boundary — present and ordered. A draft missing any required section fails the structural reviewer and FC04, and the verdict names the missing section. The jury does not return all-PASS, so the brief cannot reach Phase 5.
expectations: Plan requires all five required sections (Status, Problem Statement, User Outcome, User Journeys, Scope Boundary) present and in order
Plan notes the structural-format reviewer checks required-section presence at Phase 4
Plan notes shirabe validate FC04 rejects a brief missing a required section and names the missing section
Plan describes a missing-section draft failing the jury (not all-PASS) so it cannot reach Phase 5

evals.name: invalid-status-rejection
evals.expected_output: The frontmatter status must be one of Draft, Accepted, Done (FC02). The structural-format reviewer and shirabe validate reject a status value outside that set (for example Published) and the error lists the valid statuses. The body ## Status first non-blank line must be the bare status word matching the frontmatter status (FC03).
expectations: Plan requires the frontmatter status to be one of Draft, Accepted, Done (FC02)
Plan notes shirabe validate FC02 rejects a status value outside the valid set and lists the valid statuses
Plan notes the body ## Status first non-blank line must be the bare status word matching the frontmatter status (FC03)
Plan notes prose on the ## Status first line breaks FC03

Plan invokes shirabe transition to perform the transition
Plan targets transitioning from Draft to Accepted status

evals.name: topic-slug-validation
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 rejects the topic slug because it does not match [a-z0-9-]+. The skill stops before drafting and reports the constraint to the user. No BRIEF document is created.
expectations: Plan validates the topic slug against the [a-z0-9-]+ constraint at Phase 0
Plan rejects the input because the slug contains forbidden characters (., /)
Plan stops before drafting begins
Plan does NOT create a BRIEF document
Plan explains the slug constraint to the user

evals.name: prd-upstream-rejection
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 rejects the PRD path instead of treating it as an upstream. A PRD is downstream of a BRIEF in the tactical chain (ROADMAP -> BRIEF -> PRD), so deriving the feature's framing out of the PRD's requirements inverts the chain. The rejection message names the offending path, explains the inversion, and points the author at writing the brief from the feature topic or from the ROADMAP entry that names it. No BRIEF document is created and Phase 1 never runs.
expectations: Plan rejects the PRD path rather than accepting it as the BRIEF's upstream
Plan explains that a PRD is downstream of a BRIEF (chain runs ROADMAP -> BRIEF -> PRD) so using it as upstream inverts the chain
Plan points the author at writing the brief from the feature topic or from the ROADMAP entry that names the feature
Plan stops at Phase 0 without entering Phase 1 discovery
Plan does NOT create a BRIEF document
Plan does NOT offer to proceed with the PRD as upstream anyway

evals.name: jury-disagreement-carries-a-recommendation
evals.prompt: /brief search-filters -- the Phase 4 jury returns a content-quality verdict calling User Journey 3 a duplicate of Journey 1, and a structural-format verdict that reads the same two journeys as distinct.
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.3 hits the reviewers-disagree row. The plan quotes both verdicts, then states which reading is better supported and why, citing the specific verdict finding that decides it (the journeys' differing entry points, or the shared outcome that collapses them). The recommendation is made even though the reviewers split; the user overrides if they disagree. If the two readings are genuinely balanced, the plan says so explicitly, still recommends one, and names the tiebreaker.
expectations: Plan surfaces both reviewer perspectives rather than silently picking one
Plan states which perspective it finds better supported instead of leaving the call to the user unaided
Plan's reasoning cites the specific verdict finding that decides the disagreement, not the fact that the reviewers disagreed
Plan says so explicitly and names a tiebreaker if the two perspectives are genuinely balanced, rather than manufacturing a preference
Plan preserves the user's ability to override the recommendation
Plan does NOT present the disagreement as 'user decides' with no recommendation attached

evals.name: phase-2-questions-carry-recommended-answers
evals.prompt: /brief onboarding-checklist -- Phase 2 has written Problem Statement and User Outcome, and step 2.7 needs to surface a tradeoff-shaped framing question to the author.
evals.expected_output: Step 2.7 surfaces the framing question with a recommended answer marked '(Recommended)', grounded in what Phase 1 discovery turned up -- the upstream artifact, issue, or conversation detail that decides it -- with each alternative carrying a short reason for ranking lower. The question targets the framing rather than rehashing the draft. If discovery does not favor an answer, the plan says so, still recommends one, and names the tiebreaker.
expectations: Plan marks one answer '(Recommended)' rather than offering the framing alternatives unranked
Plan grounds the recommended answer in a specific Phase 1 discovery detail (upstream artifact, issue, or conversation), not in an abstract tradeoff list
Plan gives each alternative a short reason for ranking lower
Plan still asks the author, treating the recommendation as overridable rather than as the decision
Plan does NOT ask a rehash question such as 'does the Problem Statement look right?'
Plan does NOT present the framing alternatives side by side with no stated preference

evals.name: upstream-flag
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 parses --upstream and its value out of $ARGUMENTS before classifying the remainder, so the entry mode is freeform and the topic slug is 'inline-diff' derived from the positional argument alone -- never from the ROADMAP's filename. The value is canonicalized, bounds-checked, confined to docs/roadmaps/, confirmed to have a ROADMAP- basename (a PRD- basename gets the chain-inversion rejection on the flag exactly as it does positionally), and confirmed not to be under wip/. The tracked-by-git check does NOT run on the grounding path: it is a record-time check and the roadmap is only read. The path is stored as the context file's ## Grounding Path, Phase 1 grounds the problem/outcome candidate in it, and step 0.3a resolves the recordable upstream by reading that roadmap's own upstream: -- one hop, terminating on a STRATEGY or a VISION. The resolved value DOES take the full record-time set, tracked-by-git included, and the visibility check. Phase 2 writes it into docs/briefs/BRIEF-inline-diff.md, or omits the field when the resolution found nothing. The run says what was recorded and why it is not the roadmap. A bare --upstream with no value would be rejected at Phase 0 naming the missing argument.
expectations: Plan detects and parses the --upstream flag from $ARGUMENTS
Plan derives the topic slug 'inline-diff' from the positional argument, NOT from the ROADMAP basename
Plan validates the --upstream value: canonicalized, inside the working tree, under docs/roadmaps/, ROADMAP- basename, not under wip/
Plan records the roadmap as ## Grounding Path and writes the resolved STRATEGY or VISION into the BRIEF frontmatter, never the roadmap path
Plan announces which document was recorded and why it is not the roadmap
Plan produces docs/briefs/BRIEF-inline-diff.md rather than BRIEF-editor.md
